title: Deutsche Bank Sees Major Reckoning Ahead for AI Investors
source_used: Yahoo Finance article (commentary on the Deutsche Bank Research Institute report), read in full
key_facts: Deutsche Bank says AI could theoretically reach superintelligence by 2030, but only if model scaling continues, AI systems learn to improve themselves and the industry overcomes constraints on power, infrastructure and financing.
Training a hypothetical AGI-like model could need $300 billion to $500 billion of infrastructure and roughly 6 gigawatts of power.

Running an equivalent training cycle in four months on Nvidia Vera Rubin chips could need about 7.8 million chips and 26 gigawatts, costing about $900 billion at today's prices; a comparable cluster could fall to about $200 billion by 2030 if efficiency gains continue.
Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle are expected to invest almost $800 billion in capital expenditure this year, possibly more than $1 trillion a year through 2030.
The bank stressed the AI investment case does not require superintelligence; AI-economy revenue outside China could exceed $200 billion in 2026, up from under $1 billion in 2022.
Deutsche Bank highlighted growing pressure on hyperscaler free cash flow as capital spending rises.
quote_evidence: Deutsche Bank says artificial intelligence could theoretically reach superintelligence by 2030, but only if model scaling continues, AI systems learn to improve themselves and the industry can overcome enormous constraints around power, infrastructure and financing.
Deutsche Bank estimates that training a hypothetical AGI-like model could require $300 billion to $500 billion of infrastructure and roughly 6 gigawatts of power.
Yet the bank stressed that the AI investment case does not require superintelligence.
why_it_matters_hint: A major bank prices the infrastructure and power needed for superintelligence and flags pressure on big spenders' cash flow.
event_date: not stated (Deutsche Bank Research Institute report; Yahoo article of 13 Oct 2026)
notes: The Yahoo Finance article mixes the bank's findings with the writer's own first-person view ('I think...', 'I would watch...'); only the bank's findings are used. The Deutsche Bank report itself was not found. The headline's 'major reckoning' is Yahoo's wording.
